newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan envoy says Lima crisis near solution.
newsitem.headline: Japan envoy says Lima crisis near solution.

text.p: Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Masahiko Komura, just back from talks on the Lima hostage crisis, said on Monday he believed the time was ripe to end the standoff.

Komura, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's personal envoy, visited Peru, Cuba and the Dominican Republic over the past week to get momentum going again in talks with rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"The situation may appear deadlocked at first sight, but I am convinced that the issue is heading towards a solution," Komura told reporters.
"I think the time is ripe for a peaceful settlement," he added.
In Komura's visits to Cuba and the Dominican Republic, the governments of both countries agreed to give asylum to the hostage takers if it would help end the nearly 14-week-old siege.
Negotiations between Peru and rebels from the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) are stalled over rebel demands that imprisoned comrades should be freed as part of a hostage deal.
The MRTA rebels stormed the residence last December 17, initially taking hundreds of guests hostage. They have since released all but 72 of them.
